doc.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022

title: Utica Free Academy, teacher Ed Hacker and drum teacher George Glaskins
summary: The Zito name at school, teacher Ed Hacker, and rudimental lessons with Glaskins.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Were you a big deal, did you go to UFA?
Okay so I’m imagining that you were a big deal. “Ronnie has a gig.”

You know it’s funny, my family was, the Zito name was a big deal because my brothers went to that school and they’d say, “Oh Ronnie Zito’s coming in, we’re going to get another Zito.” And that would put me under pressure man. I’d be like oh no, because I was the youngest you know. And it was great, it was great. We had great music teachers. Ed Hacker, a great, great guy. As a matter of fact I was playing like one of the — someone paged me at the stage door after the show “Chicago” and I go to the stage door man, and it’s Ed Hacker — my old high school teacher. “Ronnie, oh I’m so proud of you.” You know I said, “Wow I can’t believe this.” Ed Hacker.
Ronnie, did you study with the drum teacher that Jimmy Wormworth did, Babe something?

No, not Babe Costello, no. It was George Glaskins. That’s who we both studied with. It was great man. I mean he didn’t know anything about jazz or anything like that, or playing a drumset, but he really, rudimentally, he was wonderful you know. And I still think about him, you know, like the way he did things when I went to his lesson you know, we’d have two practice pads set up and he’d — you know he had a beautiful roll man. I’m still working on that. And I think of him all the time.
